The first build you can just download. Grab the zip for your system below, unzip it anywhere and
double-click `usnfetch.exe`. It settles in next to the clock and opens the web page in your
browser, and a short setup walks you through adding your Usenet provider.

## New: filter the catalog by launcher and device

Once a catalog grows to a few hundred builds, most of the time you only care about the ones that
will run on one particular box. So the catalog has two more menus next to the sources:

- **Launcher:** Batocera, RetroBat, LaunchBox, HyperSpin, RetroPie, Recalbox, KNULLI, CoinOPS,
  TeknoParrot and a few more.
- **Device:** PC, Steam Deck, ROG Ally and the other handheld PCs, Raspberry Pi 3, 4 and 5,
  Anbernic and other retro handhelds, Odroid boards, and consoles (Xbox 360, Wii, XStation,
  GDEMU…). "Any Raspberry Pi" and "Any handheld PC" catch every model at once.

There's nothing to tag by hand. usnfetch reads it from the titles and labels, however they spell
it: "Raspberry Pi 5", "RPi5" and "-RPI5-" all come out as Raspberry Pi 5, and "XBOXALLYX" is a ROG
Ally. Builds for Windows-only launchers like LaunchBox or HyperSpin count as PC even when the title
doesn't say so.

Every entry shows its launcher and device as little chips. Click one to see only those, click it
again to go back. You can sort by launcher or device too, and search knows about them, so typing
"steam deck" finds the builds labelled STEAMDECK. For scripts,
`GET /api/catalog?launcher=batocera&device=raspberry pi` does the same thing.

## Fixed: memory

Some shares are one enormous disk image rather than lots of files. Opening one of those (an 8 TB
image in about 11 million pieces) pushed usnfetch to around 4 GB of memory, and it hung on to most
of it afterwards. It now peaks at about 500 MB and settles back down once the share is ready.

- Download jobs on shares with millions of files no longer load the whole file list in one go.
- Memory goes back to Windows right after a big share loads or a job finishes, instead of
  trickling back over several minutes.
- The System page has a Memory card showing how much usnfetch is using and where it goes.

## Also

- `usnfetch version` prints the version.
- The System page now says who made it.
